title: Nanaimo Bars
subtitle: Canada's no-bake classic: chocolate coconut crumb base, custard buttercream middle, snappy chocolate top
imageAlt: Nanaimo bars cut into squares showing the crumb base, custard middle and chocolate top, on a white plate
servingsNote: 16 bars from a 20 cm (8-inch) pan: 2 each

beforeYouStart.text: Soften the butter for the middle layer and have everything measured: each layer goes on as soon as the last one is firm.
About 75 minutes of fridge time between layers is built into the time.

steps.title: Line the pan
steps.text: Line a 20 cm (8-inch) square pan with parchment, leaving an overhang on two sides to lift the bars out.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: In a heatproof bowl set over a pot of barely simmering water (or a heavy saucepan on low), melt the butter with the sugar and cocoa. Whisk in the beaten egg and stir constantly 2–3 minutes, until thick and glossy; it should reach 71°C (160°F).

steps.title: Press the base
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the graham crumbs, coconut and almonds. Press firmly and evenly into the pan with the bottom of a measuring cup. Chill 15 minutes.

steps.title: Middle layer
steps.text: Beat the soft butter, cream, custard powder and icing sugar until light and smooth, about 2 minutes. Spread evenly over the base and chill 30 minutes, until firm.

steps.title: Chocolate top
steps.text: Melt the chocolate and butter together over low heat (or in the microwave in 20-second bursts), stirring until smooth. Cool 5 minutes so it's pourable but not hot, then spread it over the middle layer. Chill 30 minutes.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Lift the slab out and let it sit 5 minutes. Cut into 16 squares with a sharp knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry between cuts, so the layers stay clean.

fixIt.fix: Let the slab sit out 5–10 minutes first, and use a hot, dry knife.
Beat in more icing sugar, 2 tbsp at a time, and chill longer.
Press it harder, and make sure the egg mixture cooked until thick before adding the crumbs.

saleTip: Graham crumbs, coconut and baking chocolate are all on the baking aisle at No Frills and usually on sale together in December.
swap: No almonds? Use walnuts, or leave them out: the bars hold together fine. Vanilla pudding powder works in place of custard powder.
leftovers: They keep beautifully. Keep a few in the freezer for a treat straight from the cold.
doneness: Each layer should be firm before the next goes on. The base is cooked once it's thick and glossy (71°C / 160°F), which makes the egg safe.
source: Based on the City of Nanaimo's official Nanaimo bar recipe (Joyce Hardcastle, 1986): cooked cocoa-egg base with graham, coconut and nuts; custard buttercream; chocolate top.
prepAhead: Make them up to a week ahead and keep in the fridge, or freeze the slab uncut up to 3 months.
reheat: Not needed. Serve cold, or let them sit 5 minutes out of the fridge.

basic.note: No nuts, and milk in the middle instead of cream.

stepNotes.2: Basic: graham crumbs and coconut only.
stepNotes.3: Basic: use milk in place of the cream.

fancy.note: Candy cane Nanaimo bars: peppermint in the middle layer, crushed candy canes on top.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: beat in the peppermint extract with the custard powder.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: scatter the crushed candy canes over the chocolate right after spreading.

plating: Cut smaller, 25 squares, for a dessert tray.
Serve fridge-cold on a white plate so the layers show.
Wipe the knife between every cut.

why.0-3: Cooking the egg into the cocoa butter binds the base and makes it safe.
why.1-2: Custard powder gives the middle its colour and vanilla custard flavour.
why.2-1: A little butter in the chocolate keeps it from shattering when you cut.

funFact: Named for Nanaimo, B.C. In 1986 the city held a contest for the ultimate recipe; Joyce Hardcastle's won, and it's still the official one.

keeps.note: wrap the uncut slab or the bars well
keeps.thaw: Overnight in the fridge; cut while still cold
